# Quality Control {#mx-qc}

**Location:** Methylomics \> Quality Control &nbsp;|&nbsp; **Group:** Data

The **Quality Control** module performs the standard set of QC checks on an uploaded (or preloaded) methylation dataset — sample call rate, probe detection, sex concordance, batch structure, and multivariate outlier detection — before any downstream normalization or differential analysis is run. It is organized as a dashboard with a persistent status summary at the top and eight sub-tabs, each covering one stage of the QC pipeline. This chapter is a fully worked example of how every module chapter in this guide should read once finished — use it as the template for the remaining chapters.

```{r mxqc-fig-dashboard, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="The live QC dashboard: cohort composition, PCA outliers & chrY sex-check, and the probe-filtering cascade, all summarized above the sub-tabs."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-1.png")
```

Above the sub-tabs, three cards give an at-a-glance summary that updates live as filters are changed further down: **Cohort composition** (sample counts by group/sex), **PCA outliers & chrY sex-check** (how many samples flagged so far), and the **Probe-filtering cascade** (how many probes survive each filtering step).

## Overview

The **Overview** sub-tab shows the loaded dataset (source, dimensions, and a basic pass/fail QC status) and, for datasets with a sex covariate, the currently selected subgroup. Use this tab to confirm the correct dataset is active before drilling into any of the more detailed QC checks.

## Sample QC

**Sample QC** computes a call-rate QC pass/fail per sample and exposes the options used to compute it, plus a table for manually including or excluding specific samples regardless of their automatic call-rate status. Users can change the display by adjusting the call-rate threshold and immediately see which samples move in or out of the "pass" set.

```{r mxqc-fig-samples, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Sample call-rate QC options and the manual sample inclusion/exclusion table."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-2.png")
```

[Describe the call-rate threshold control, its default value, and what "manual inclusion/exclusion" overrides.]

## Probe QC

**Probe QC** filters probes by detection call rate and other standard exclusion criteria (e.g. cross-reactive or SNP-overlapping probes, depending on what the underlying pipeline applies). A summary chart and a probe-retention flowchart show how many probes are removed at each step, and the filtered probe-by-sample matrix can be downloaded directly from this tab.

```{r mxqc-fig-probes, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Probe filtering options, the filtering summary chart, and the probe retention flowchart."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-3.png")
```

## Sex QC

**Sex QC** checks reported sex against methylation-inferred sex using X- vs. Y-chromosome methylation signal, flagging discordant samples in a dedicated table alongside a scatter plot of X vs. Y methylation.

```{r mxqc-fig-sex, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Sex check results table and the X vs. Y methylation scatter plot, with discordant samples highlighted."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-4.png")
```

[Note what happens to a sample flagged as discordant — is it auto-excluded, or does the user decide?]

## Batch QC

**Batch QC** corrects for a specified batch covariate (e.g. array/chip/plate) using [ComBat / RUVm — confirm which method(s) are exposed and how the user selects between them], and shows PCA before vs. after correction plus a table of variance explained by the top principal components, so the user can visually confirm the batch effect has been reduced without over-correcting biological signal.

```{r mxqc-fig-batch, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="PCA before vs. after batch correction, and the variance-explained table for the top PCs."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-5.png")
```

## Outlier QC

**Outlier QC** flags multivariate outlier samples using PCA distance from the group centroid and a hierarchical clustering dendrogram, with adjustable detection settings and a ranked outlier score table.

```{r mxqc-fig-outlier, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Outlier detection settings, the ranked outlier score table, PCA sample structure, and the sample dendrogram."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-6.png")
```

## Visualizations

For datasets uploaded from raw IDAT files, **Visualizations** additionally shows detection p-value distributions, bead count distributions, and a control-probe heatmap — array-level QC diagnostics that aren't available once data arrives as a pre-computed beta-value matrix.

```{r mxqc-fig-viz, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Detection p-value distribution, bead count distribution, and control-probe heatmap (raw IDAT uploads only)."}
# knitr::include_graphics("Figures/f20-7.png")
```
